properties.rationale:
Anthony's standing policy from 2026-07-23, unchanged: validation for this project is the trials programme — reflow2 used on real designs, logged in docs/trials/ and docs/trials-private/ (the brownfield ophyd-service pass, the greenfield aidrone pass) plus sustained real use of the StoryFlow fleet. Formal validation-kind Verification nodes are not this project's tracking mechanism, and recording 68 near-identical ones would turn the number green without anyone having checked anything — the dishonesty `dec:passing-is-verified` exists to prevent.

ACCEPTED AT 68 CAPABILITIES, and the count is recorded here on purpose: this gap's id is now keyed on its RULE rather than its member set (`dec:aggregate-gap-keyed-on-rule`), so this acknowledgement CARRIES as the design grows instead of expiring on every addition. That is the fix for the churn — the same disposition had been re-recorded about twenty times, at 33, 34, 35 … 65, 67 and 68 capabilities. The trade-off is deliberate: a capability added tomorrow is covered by this judgement without a fresh look, which is what a standing disposition means. The growth stays VISIBLE without the churn, by comparing the count named here against the count in the live gap's title — if that gap says 90 and this says 68, twenty-two capabilities joined under a judgement made when there were 68, and whether that still holds is a question a reader can now actually ask.

This should be the last acknowledgement this gap ever needs. If it re-fires because the id moved again, the keying regressed and `an_aggregate_gaps_id_does_not_move_when_the_population_grows` should have caught it.
